text.paragraph: Five-and-a-half-month review: A1c, lipids, walking distance, the revascularization decision, foot and eye follow-up. [S]

Ms. Fitzgerald returns eleven weeks after her three-month visit. She stepped up to semaglutide 0.5 mg weekly in September; she had mild nausea for the first two weeks, which passed, and she has lost 1.5 kg. Her glucose monitor shows time in range 74% and time below 70 mg/dL 0.6%, with no reading below 54 mg/dL. She finished the supervised exercise program and walks most days; she can now walk about five blocks before calf pain, and only climbing slows her. She has no rest pain and no sores. She has had five right-eye injections and the interval is now eight weeks. The podiatrist saw her in September. She has had no bleeding. Her mammogram in July was normal, and the bone density scan is booked between tours. She feels ready for her winter tour. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-26; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 80.6 kg, BMI 29.6; blood pressure 120/68, pulse 60
Skin intact; minimal callus; hammer toes; no ulcer; monofilament felt at all sites; right foot pulses absent, left faint; feet warm
Best-corrected acuity 75 letters right and 81 letters left

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral artery disease: cramping in both calves after about one and a half blocks of walking, worse on the right, easing within minutes of rest; no rest pain, wounds, or color change. Resting ankle-brachial index 0.62 right and 0.74 left, toe-brachial index 0.46 and 0.55; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right and faint on the left. A1c 8.6% on metformin, glipizide and glargine, with low glucose readings (to 52 mg/dL) after late performances. Foot: protective sensation intact to the 10-g monofilament at all sites and to vibration; callus under the second metatarsal heads; hammer toes of the second and third toes; no ulcer (IWGDF risk category 2). Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetes and its circulatory complications
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the type of diabetes was not made public and is synthetic.

Moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with center-involving diabetic macular edema in the right eye (best-corrected acuity 64 letters, about 20/50) and moderate nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema in the left eye (81 letters); lens implants in both eyes from earlier cataract surgery. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetic eye problems
S — Synthetic modern eye diagnosis on retinal imaging and optical coherence tomography in the clinic; the left eye is described in the display.

Coronary artery disease after five-vessel coronary bypass surgery last year, with an intensive care stay; no angina now; on aspirin, a statin, and metoprolol. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented heart surgery
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented heart surgery; bypass grafts are described in the display.

Type 2 diabetes with peripheral artery disease (E11.51). A1c 7.1%, at her goal below 7.5%, with no level 2 or 3 lows. After supervised exercise she walks about five blocks, and claudication no longer limits her daily life or her performing, so revascularization is not needed now; Dr. Okafor-Lane agrees by message. Creatinine 0.94 mg/dL, eGFR 65, potassium 4.5 mmol/L. [S]
Continue metformin, empagliflozin, semaglutide 0.5 mg weekly, and glargine 24 units.
Walk at least three times a week for life.
Vascular review with ankle-brachial index and duplex next month, as planned.
Podiatry every three months; foot check at every visit.

Coronary artery disease after bypass surgery (I25.10). LDL 48 mg/dL, at goal, on atorvastatin 80 mg and ezetimibe; total cholesterol 114, HDL 47, triglycerides 96 mg/dL. [S]
Continue atorvastatin, ezetimibe, aspirin, rivaroxaban, and metoprolol.
Lipid panel yearly.

Immunizations. Influenza and recombinant zoster vaccines due this autumn, as planned at the wellness visit. [S]
High-dose influenza vaccine and recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 given today; zoster dose 2 in two to six months; COVID-19 and RSV vaccines at her pharmacy before the winter tour.

Diabetic macular edema, right eye (E11.3311). Acuity 75 letters, from 64 at intake; no worsening of retinopathy reported by the retina clinic since semaglutide began. [S]
Continue retina-clinic treatment every eight weeks; left eye examined at each visit.
